chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Jamil ibn Durraj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), saying:
God has not tested the servants with anything harder for them than the giving of the dirham.
ai.seo_question: What is considered the hardest test for humans according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the voluntary expenditure of wealth (infaq) as the most arduous test for believers, surpassing even physical hardships. This highlights the spiritual struggle against *bukhl* (stinginess) and the purification of the soul through detachment from material possessions, a core theme in Shia ethical teachings.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-27 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz, on the authority of Jamil ibn Dur’raj that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
God has not tested the servants with anything harder than giving money.”
